decisions.reason: Connects session→host→tool-worker→npm to the replaced package tree; host death kills the result transport and outcome stays unknown; frames this in-session self-upgrade as structurally fatal without a universal every-platform claim (separately notes Windows EBUSY locking).

Shims written only at install end: old displaced, new never generated; dsh/dsh.cmd missing, dsh.ps1 stale into the old tree; content irrelevant to command resolution; the hand-swap made the tree non-standard and hand repair is rejected per the skill rule.
Repair notes' pinned external reinstall regenerated all three shims with dsh --version = rc.1; checkout retagged to rc.1; recorded repair and deferred real-machine verification kept separate.

Recognition test, refusal to execute the global install, stop-everything-first (browser refresh explicitly not a stop), exact pin justified via dist-tag lag, restart/refresh/verify; known skill rules distinguished from incident-specific findings; handoff is a plain external shell, not a dependent tool of the dying host.

Pre-execution self-reference guard tying the target to the running host's package path; version-only diff rules out re-migration; checklist covers version markers, plugin loading, ghost processes, checkout alignment, backup cleanup after confirmation; no code change demanded.

caps.reason: Final protocol hands off to an external pinned install; in-session execution is explicitly rejected in every form including detached/background.
Manual swaps/shims are diagnosed as harmful and rejected; the sanctioned repair is the pinned formal re-install.
